tasks.title: Phase 0: Project Initialization with Remix, Prisma, and Tailwind CSS
tasks.description: Set up a new Remix project, integrate Prisma for database access, and configure Tailwind CSS for styling. This forms the foundational infrastructure of the Orbit application.
tasks.details: Use the Remix CLI to bootstrap the project: `npx create-remix@latest`. During setup, select TypeScript. Afterwards, add Tailwind CSS following the official Remix guide. Initialize Prisma with `npx prisma init` and set the provider to `postgresql` in `prisma/schema.prisma`.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the Remix dev server runs successfully (`npm run dev`). Check that a basic page with Tailwind classes (e.g., `bg-blue-500`) renders correctly. Ensure `npx prisma` commands execute without errors.

subtasks.title: Bootstrap New Remix Project with TypeScript
subtasks.description: Create the initial project structure using the official Remix CLI. This task establishes the foundational file system and configuration for the application.
subtasks.details: Execute the command `npx create-remix@latest` in your terminal. During the interactive setup, ensure you select 'TypeScript' as the language choice. Name the project 'orbit' or as per project convention.
subtasks.testStrategy: After creation, navigate into the project directory, run `npm install`, and then `npm run dev`. Verify that the default Remix welcome page loads successfully in a web browser at the specified localhost port.

subtasks.title: Integrate and Configure Tailwind CSS
subtasks.description: Add Tailwind CSS to the project for utility-first styling, following the official integration guide for Remix.
subtasks.details: Install the necessary dev dependencies: `tailwindcss`, `postcss`, and `autoprefixer`. Run `npx tailwindcss init -p` to generate `tailwind.config.ts` and `postcss.config.js`. Configure the `content` path in `tailwind.config.ts` to include `app/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`.
subtasks.testStrategy:
Modify the root route (`app/routes/_index.tsx`) to include an element with a Tailwind class, such as `

Hello

`. Run the dev server and verify that the text color is blue.

subtasks.title: Initialize Prisma ORM
subtasks.description: Set up Prisma in the project to prepare for database integration. This step creates the necessary Prisma configuration files.
subtasks.details: Run the command `npx prisma init` in the project's root directory. This will create a new `prisma` directory containing a `schema.prisma` file, and it will add a `DATABASE_URL` variable to your `.env` file.
subtasks.testStrategy: Confirm the existence of the `prisma/schema.prisma` file and the `.env` file. Run `npx prisma -h` to ensure the Prisma CLI is installed and executable within the project.

subtasks.title: Configure Prisma Schema for PostgreSQL
subtasks.description: Update the Prisma schema to specify PostgreSQL as the database provider and set the connection URL.
subtasks.details: Edit the `prisma/schema.prisma` file. Locate the `datasource db` block and change the `provider` field from its default to `"postgresql"`. Then, edit the `.env` file to set the `DATABASE_URL` to your actual PostgreSQL connection string.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the command `npx prisma validate` to check the syntax of your schema and the format of the database URL. The command should complete successfully without any validation errors.

subtasks.title: Create Prisma Client Singleton and Verify Connection
subtasks.description: Implement a reusable Prisma Client instance and create a test route to verify that the application can successfully connect to and query the database.
subtasks.details: Create a utility file `app/utils/db.server.ts` to export a singleton instance of `PrismaClient`. Add a temporary `model Test { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) }` to `schema.prisma`. Run `npx prisma db push` to sync the schema with the database. Create a loader in a route that uses the client to perform a simple query, such as a `count()` on the Test model, and render the result.
subtasks.testStrategy: Access the test route in a browser. The page should load without connection errors and display the result of the database query (e.g., 'Count: 0'). This will confirm that Remix, Tailwind, and Prisma are all correctly integrated.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down the task of initializing a new Remix project with Prisma and Tailwind CSS into sequential steps. Start with bootstrapping the Remix app, then integrate Tailwind, set up Prisma, configure the database connection, and finally create a test route to verify the entire stack.

tasks.title: Phase 0: Configure Database Connection
tasks.description: Create the database server utility file to manage a singleton instance of the Prisma client, ensuring efficient database connections.
tasks.details: Create a file `app/utils/db.server.ts`. This file will instantiate and export a single PrismaClient instance for the entire application to prevent connection exhaustion in a serverless environment. Example: `import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'; let db: PrismaClient; declare global { var __db: PrismaClient | undefined; } if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') { db = new PrismaClient(); } else { if (!global.__db) { global.__db = new PrismaClient(); } db = global.__db; } export { db };`
tasks.testStrategy: Create a temporary test route that imports `db` and attempts a simple query like `db.$connect()`. The route should load without crashing the server.

subtasks.title: Install Prisma Client Package
subtasks.description: Ensure the `@prisma/client` package is installed as a project dependency to allow interaction with the database.
subtasks.details: Run the command `npm install @prisma/client` in the terminal. This will add the package to the `package.json` file and install it in `node_modules`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that `@prisma/client` is present in the `dependencies` section of the `package.json` file.

subtasks.title: Generate Prisma Client from Schema
subtasks.description: Generate the type-safe Prisma Client based on the defined models in the `prisma/schema.prisma` file. This step is necessary before the client can be imported in the application code.
subtasks.details: Execute the Prisma CLI command `npx prisma generate`. This command reads the schema file and creates the necessary client files inside `node_modules/@prisma/client`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the command and ensure it completes without errors. Check the console output for a success message indicating the client was generated.

subtasks.title: Create Database Utility File
subtasks.description: Create a new TypeScript file within the `app/utils` directory to encapsulate the database connection logic. The `.server.ts` suffix ensures it's only included in the server bundle.
subtasks.details: Create a new file named `db.server.ts` inside the `app/utils/` directory. This file will house the singleton instance of the Prisma client.
subtasks.testStrategy: Confirm the existence of the file at the path `app/utils/db.server.ts` in the project structure.

subtasks.title: Implement Prisma Client Singleton Pattern
subtasks.description: Implement the singleton pattern for `PrismaClient` in `db.server.ts` to prevent creating multiple client instances, which can exhaust database connections, especially in a serverless or development environment with hot-reloading.
subtasks.details: Add the following code to `app/utils/db.server.ts`: `import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'; let db: PrismaClient; declare global { var __db: PrismaClient | undefined; } if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') { db = new PrismaClient(); } else { if (!global.__db) { global.__db = new PrismaClient(); } db = global.__db; } export { db };`
subtasks.testStrategy: Perform a code review on `app/utils/db.server.ts` to ensure the singleton pattern is correctly implemented and the `db` instance is exported.

subtasks.title: Create Temporary Test Route for Connection Verification
subtasks.description: Create a temporary Remix route to import the database client and execute a simple query. This will serve as a functional test to confirm that the database connection is configured correctly and accessible.
subtasks.details: Create a new route file, e.g., `app/routes/_test.db.tsx`. In the `loader` function, import `{ db }` from `~/utils/db.server.ts` and attempt a connection with `await db.$connect()`. Return a success JSON response. The leading underscore in the route name prevents it from matching a URL path.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the development server and access a page in the application. The application should load without crashing. Check the server-side console logs for any connection errors to confirm a successful connection.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down the task of setting up a Prisma client singleton. Steps should include installing the client, generating it from the schema, creating the `db.server.ts` utility file, implementing the singleton pattern for development vs. production, and creating a test route to verify the connection.

tasks.title: Phase 0: Base Validation Schema Setup with Zod
tasks.description: Configure Zod for data validation, including setting up custom error messages in Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR) for a consistent user experience.
tasks.details: Install Zod: `npm install zod`. Create a utility file `app/utils/validation.server.ts`. In this file, configure a custom Zod error map to translate default error messages to PT-BR. Export the configured Zod instance for use in other schemas. `import { z } from 'zod'; import { zodI18nMap } from 'zod-i18n-map'; import pt from 'zod-i18n-map/locales/pt/zod.json'; z.setErrorMap(zodI18nMap(pt)); export { z as zValidated };`
tasks.testStrategy: Create a unit test using Vitest. Define a simple schema, parse invalid data, and assert that the thrown error message is in PT-BR.

subtasks.title: Install Zod and i18n Dependencies
subtasks.description: Add the required 'zod' and 'zod-i18n-map' packages to the project's dependencies to enable validation and internationalization of error messages.
subtasks.details: Execute the command `npm install zod zod-i18n-map` in the project's root directory. Verify that the packages are correctly added to `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npm install` and check `package.json` to ensure `zod` and `zod-i18n-map` are listed as dependencies.

subtasks.title: Create Zod Configuration Utility File
subtasks.description: Create a new server-side utility file to house the global Zod configuration, ensuring a centralized place for validation logic.
subtasks.details: Create a new file at the path `app/utils/validation.server.ts`. This file will contain the Zod setup and custom error mapping.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that the file `app/utils/validation.server.ts` exists in the file system.

subtasks.title: Configure Zod Custom Error Map for PT-BR
subtasks.description: Implement the Zod configuration to override the default error messages with Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR) translations using 'zod-i18n-map'.
subtasks.details: In `app/utils/validation.server.ts`, import `z`, `zodI18nMap`, and the `pt` locale. Use `z.setErrorMap(zodI18nMap(pt))` to set the global error map for all subsequent Zod schemas.
subtasks.testStrategy: Code review to ensure the `setErrorMap` function is called correctly with the Portuguese locale data.

subtasks.title: Export the Configured Zod Instance
subtasks.description: Export the globally configured Zod instance under the alias 'zValidated' to be used throughout the application for consistent validation.
subtasks.details: In `app/utils/validation.server.ts`, add the export statement: `export { z as zValidated };`. This makes the PT-BR configured instance available for import in other modules.
subtasks.testStrategy: Attempt to import `{ zValidated }` from `app/utils/validation.server.ts` in another file to ensure it resolves correctly.

subtasks.title: Write Unit Test for Zod PT-BR Error Messages
subtasks.description: Create a Vitest unit test to confirm that the custom error map is working correctly and that Zod schemas produce error messages in Brazilian Portuguese.
subtasks.details: Create a test file, e.g., `app/utils/validation.server.test.ts`. Import `zValidated`. Define a simple schema like `zValidated.string().email()`. Use `schema.safeParse()` with an invalid email address and assert that the returned error message is in PT-BR (e.g., contains 'E-mail inválido').
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npm test` and verify that the test case passes, confirming that the error message is correctly translated to Portuguese.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Outline the steps to configure Zod with PT-BR error messages. Subtasks should include installing dependencies (`zod`, `zod-i18n-map`), creating the central validation utility file, implementing the custom error map, exporting the configured instance, and writing a unit test to verify the Portuguese error messages.

tasks.title: Phase 0: Implement Core Security Headers and CSP
tasks.description: Establish baseline security by implementing essential security headers, including a Content Security Policy (CSP), to protect against common web vulnerabilities.
tasks.details: Create `app/utils/security.server.ts`. This file will export functions to generate security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, etc.) and a strict CSP. These headers will be applied in the root layout's `headers` export in `app/root.tsx`.
tasks.testStrategy: Use browser developer tools to inspect the response headers of the application's home page. Verify that all configured security headers, including the CSP, are present and correctly formatted. Use a security scanner tool like `observatory.mozilla.org` for a quick check.

subtasks.title: Create Security Utility File
subtasks.description: Create the new file `app/utils/security.server.ts` which will serve as the central module for all security header logic.
subtasks.details: Create an empty file at `app/utils/security.server.ts`. The `.server.ts` extension ensures that this module and its dependencies will not be included in the client-side bundle.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that the file `app/utils/security.server.ts` exists in the file system after creation.

subtasks.title: Define and Export Basic Security Headers
subtasks.description: In `app/utils/security.server.ts`, add and export a set of common, non-CSP security headers to protect against clickjacking and MIME-type sniffing.
subtasks.details: Define a constant object exporting the following headers: 'X-Frame-Options': 'SAMEORIGIN', 'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff', and 'Referrer-Policy': 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin'.
subtasks.testStrategy: Perform a code review to ensure the header names and values are correct and follow security best practices.

subtasks.title: Implement a Strict Content Security Policy (CSP)
subtasks.description: In `app/utils/security.server.ts`, create a function to generate a strict Content Security Policy string. The policy must differentiate between development and production environments.
subtasks.details: Create a function that returns a CSP string. The base policy should be restrictive (e.g., 'default-src': ''self''). In development (`process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'`), the policy must be relaxed to allow for Remix's live reload and dev tools scripts.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test the function to verify it returns the correct restrictive policy for production and the more permissive policy for development.

subtasks.title: Create a Composite Headers Function
subtasks.description: In `app/utils/security.server.ts`, create and export a single function that combines the basic headers and the Content Security Policy into a single `Headers` object.
subtasks.details: Create an exported function named `getSecurityHeaders` that takes a `Headers` object as an argument. This function will merge the basic headers from subtask 2 and the CSP from subtask 3 with any headers passed into it, returning a new `Headers` object.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write a unit test for `getSecurityHeaders` that confirms it correctly merges the static headers, the CSP, and any passed-in headers without overwriting them unintentionally.

subtasks.title: Apply Security Headers in the Root Layout
subtasks.description: Integrate the security headers into the application by using the Remix `headers` export in `app/root.tsx`.
subtasks.details: Import the `getSecurityHeaders` function into `app/root.tsx`. Export a `headers` function from this file that calls `getSecurityHeaders`, passing it the `loaderHeaders` from the function arguments. This will apply the headers to every response generated by the application.
subtasks.testStrategy: After deployment, use browser developer tools to inspect the network response for the home page. Verify that all security headers, including the CSP, are present. Use an online scanner like observatory.mozilla.org to validate the implementation.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down the task of implementing security headers and a CSP in Remix. Steps should cover creating a security utility file, defining basic headers, implementing a strict but dev-friendly CSP, creating a composite function to merge all headers, and applying these headers in the root layout.

tasks.title: Phase 1: Model Core Entities in Prisma Schema
tasks.description: Define the `Tenant`, `Plan`, and `TenantFeature` data models in the `schema.prisma` file, establishing the core data structure for the application.
tasks.details: In `prisma/schema.prisma`, define the models. `Tenant` should include fields like `id`, `name`, `slug (unique)`, `domain (unique)`, `licenseKey (unique)`, `status`. `Plan` should have `id`, `name`, `features`. `TenantFeature` will be a join table linking `Tenant` and a feature string, representing overrides.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npx prisma validate` to ensure the schema is syntactically correct and all relations are properly defined.

subtasks.title: Define TenantStatus Enum and Base Tenant Model
subtasks.description: Create the `TenantStatus` enum and the initial `Tenant` model in `schema.prisma`. This model will store the core information for each tenant, including their status.
subtasks.details: In `prisma/schema.prisma`, first define a `TenantStatus` enum with values `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, and `SUSPENDED`. Then, create the `Tenant` model with the following fields: `id` (String, @id, @default(cuid())), `name` (String), `slug` (String, @unique), `domain` (String, @unique), `licenseKey` (String, @unique), `status` (TenantStatus, @default(ACTIVE)), `createdAt` (DateTime, @default(now())), and `updatedAt` (DateTime, @updatedAt).
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npx prisma format` to ensure the syntax of the new enum and model is correct.

subtasks.title: Define the Plan Model
subtasks.description: Create the `Plan` model in `schema.prisma` to represent the subscription plans available to tenants, including a list of associated features.
subtasks.details: In `prisma/schema.prisma`, add a `Plan` model. It should include the fields: `id` (String, @id, @default(cuid())), `name` (String, @unique), `features` (String[]), `createdAt` (DateTime, @default(now())), and `updatedAt` (DateTime, @updatedAt). The `features` array will store string identifiers for each feature included in the plan.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npx prisma format` after adding the model to check for any syntax errors.

subtasks.title: Establish Relationship Between Tenant and Plan
subtasks.description: Link the `Tenant` and `Plan` models to create a one-to-many relationship, allowing each tenant to be assigned to a specific plan.
subtasks.details: In `prisma/schema.prisma`, modify the `Tenant` model to add `planId String` and a relation field `plan Plan @relation(fields: [planId], references: [id])`. In the `Plan` model, add the back-relation `tenants Tenant[]`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npx prisma validate` to confirm that the foreign key and relation fields are correctly defined and resolve without ambiguity.

subtasks.title: Define TenantFeature Model for Overrides
subtasks.description: Create the `TenantFeature` model to act as a join table, allowing for specific feature overrides for individual tenants, separate from their subscribed plan.
subtasks.details: In `prisma/schema.prisma`, create the `TenantFeature` model. It will include `tenantId` (String), `feature` (String), and a `tenant` relation field `Tenant @relation(fields: [tenantId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)`. Add `@@id([tenantId, feature])` to create a composite primary key. Finally, add the back-relation `featureOverrides TenantFeature[]` to the `Tenant` model.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npx prisma validate` to check that the composite primary key and the relationship to the Tenant model are correctly configured.

subtasks.title: Finalize and Validate Full Prisma Schema
subtasks.description: Perform a final validation of the entire `schema.prisma` file after all models and relations have been defined to ensure it is syntactically and logically correct.
subtasks.details: With all models (`Tenant`, `Plan`, `TenantFeature`) and their relationships in place, execute the command `npx prisma format` to apply consistent formatting. Following that, run `npx prisma validate` to perform a comprehensive check for any errors in the schema.
subtasks.testStrategy: The successful execution of `npx prisma validate` with the output 'The schema is valid.' confirms that this task is complete.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Generate subtasks for modeling core entities in Prisma. The steps should include defining the `Tenant` model with its status enum, defining the `Plan` model, establishing the relationship between `Tenant` and `Plan`, defining the `TenantFeature` join model for overrides, and performing a final validation of the complete schema.

tasks.title: Phase 1: Generate and Run Initial Database Migration
tasks.description: Apply the defined Prisma schema to the PostgreSQL database by generating and running the initial migration.
tasks.details: Execute the command `npx prisma migrate dev --name init`. This will create the SQL migration file based on `schema.prisma` and apply it to the database configured in the `.env` file.
tasks.testStrategy: Connect to the PostgreSQL database using a client (e.g., psql, pgAdmin) and verify that the `Tenant`, `Plan`, and `TenantFeature` tables have been created with the correct columns and constraints.

subtasks.title: Confirm Database Connection URL in .env File
subtasks.description: Verify that the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable in the root `.env` file is correctly configured and points to the intended PostgreSQL development database before running any migration commands.
subtasks.details: Open the `.env` file at the project root. Check the connection string format: `postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE?schema=public`. Ensure all parts, especially the user, password, and database name, are correct.
subtasks.testStrategy: Attempt to connect to the database using the connection string with an external tool like `psql` or a GUI client to confirm credentials are valid.

subtasks.title: Perform Final Review of Prisma Schema
subtasks.description: Before generating the migration, conduct a final review of the `prisma/schema.prisma` file to ensure the models (`Tenant`, `Plan`, `TenantFeature`), fields, and relations are accurately defined.
subtasks.details: Open and inspect the `prisma/schema.prisma` file. Verify the data types, default values, relations (`@relation`), and constraints (`@id`, `@unique`) for all defined models. Ensure it reflects the intended database structure.

subtasks.title: Generate the Initial Migration File
subtasks.description: Execute the Prisma migrate command to generate the SQL migration file based on the current state of `schema.prisma`. This step creates the migration files without applying them.
subtasks.details: Run the command `npx prisma migrate dev --name init --create-only`. This will create a new migration folder under `prisma/migrations/` containing a `migration.sql` file. This allows for an optional review of the generated SQL.
subtasks.testStrategy: Check the `prisma/migrations` directory for a new folder named with a timestamp and `_init`. Verify that a `migration.sql` file exists inside it and contains SQL `CREATE TABLE` statements.

subtasks.title: Apply the Generated Migration to the Database
subtasks.description: Run the Prisma command that applies the pending 'init' migration to the development database, synchronizing its schema with the Prisma schema file.
subtasks.details: Execute the command `npx prisma migrate dev` in the terminal. Since the migration was already created, this command will detect it and apply it to the database specified in the `DATABASE_URL`.
subtasks.testStrategy: The command output should indicate that the migration was successfully applied. Check the `_prisma_migrations` table in the database to see a new entry for the 'init' migration.

subtasks.title: Verify Database Schema After Migration
subtasks.description: Connect directly to the PostgreSQL database to inspect the schema and confirm that the tables, columns, types, and constraints have been created correctly as per the migration.
subtasks.details: Use a database client (e.g., pgAdmin, DBeaver, or psql) to connect to the development database. Verify the existence and structure of the `Tenant`, `Plan`, and `TenantFeature` tables. Check column names, data types, and primary keys.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manually confirm that the schema in the database matches the models defined in `prisma/schema.prisma`. Specifically, check for the `Tenant` table and its columns.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down the process of running a database migration with Prisma. subtasks.description: Create the new file for the tenant schema and import the necessary customized Zod instance from the validation utility.
